note:
ISO 2026-W11 runs from March 9 through March 15. Venus and Saturn are separated by about 0.5° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 1.3° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌗 Last Quarter — 09:38:31 UTC. Moderate moonlight makes timing and local sky position important for faint targets. Use Avior as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -10.9; direct motion; 72.1% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Pluto in ecliptic longitude Mar 15 00:34 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude 5.1; retrograde motion; 1.2% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Mars in ecliptic longitude Mar 15 08:08 UTC. Venus: In solar glare; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 96.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: In solar glare; magnitude 1.2; direct motion; 99.3% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Mar 15 08:08 UTC. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.1; direct motion; 98.7% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.4; retrograde motion; 99.3% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Station Mar 11 03:30 UTC: turns direct. Saturn: In solar glare; magnitude 1.0; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: In solar glare; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Mar 15 00:34 UTC.

**Binoculars:** Trace Cancer’s charted figure in the finder, then identify Tarf at its charted position. Trace Chamaeleon’s charted figure in the finder, then identify α Cha at its charted position. Trace Volans’s closed figure in the finder, then identify β Vol at its charted position. Trace Pyxis’s charted figure in the finder, then identify β Pyx at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** Concentrate on Beehive Cluster. Increase magnification only after the target and surrounding pattern are secure.

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

story_candidates.dek: Tarf is a stellar reference in Cnc used by the weekly observing calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected Tarf for this week’s fixed-sky observing sequence; its permanent object identity ties the weekly entry to the same star used by the finder.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Cnc constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.
